ownership.insiderDesc: Schneider Electric has NO controlling shareholder - a broad and dispersed shareholder base, unlike Hermes or Campari in this portfolio. Employee share ownership (WESOP, Worldwide Employee Share Ownership Plan, launched in 1995 and renewed every year) estimated at ~3,7% of the capital (secondary source, see insiderSource) - this figure represents a base of stable employee shareholders and not a control block. Institutional investors ~50% of the capital (BlackRock, MFS, Vanguard and other large managers among the biggest holders, none of them individually exceeding a few percent), public/retail free float estimated at ~45%. SE-type governance (Societas Europaea) with separate Chairman of the Board (Jean-Pascal Tricoire) and Chief Executive Officer (Olivier Blum) since 2023.

items.text: Sanction by the French Competition Authority (decision of 29/10/2024): a 207 M€ fine targeting several players in electrical distribution in France, including Schneider Electric, for having restricted the pricing autonomy of certain distributors (anticompetitive practices in the commercial distribution market). Fine paid in April 2025. Schneider Electric firmly disputes the Authority's conclusions and has appealed to the Paris Court of Appeal - proceedings ongoing, outcome not known at this stage. A 104 M€ provision maintained on the balance sheet (the gap with the amount paid, tied to the challenge), a 207 M€ financial asset recognised pending the outcome of the appeal. Also: placed under formal investigation by an investigating magistrate on 07/10/2022 in the same case (a 20 M€ bank guarantee now expired, an 80 M€ cash guarantee maintained) - proceedings disputed, ongoing.

compliance.note: This is a sanction for anticompetitive practices (distribution/competition law), NOT an allegation of accounting fraud or of deception of investors/consumers in the strict sense of the compliance field as defined for this portfolio - included here out of caution and for transparency given its financially quantified character and the fact that it is still being challenged on appeal. To be removed from this field if the protocol considers this type of competition-law litigation to be out of scope; kept for now in the 'cumulative ledger' by analogy with the treatment applied to the Lagfin tax dispute on the Campari ticker (a related matter, but distinct from the entity itself).

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quarterly guidance (the group guides on the full year; next print is Q3 26 revenue on 2026-10-15). Qualitative H2 signals from the call: H2 margin phasing mechanically less favorable than H1 (productivity comparison base gets tougher - more than 70% of FY25 productivity was delivered in H2 2025 - and the EUR 100m Q2 tariff refund does not repeat); if the June price run-rate is repeated in H2, pricing would fully offset raw-material inflation plus tariffs in value; services growth contribution expected to improve in H2; Middle East uncertainty remains a headwind for both businesses in H2 26; 'triple 4' expected - all 4 end markets, 4 business models and 4 regions contributing.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 RAISED at H1 (2026-07-30): organic revenue growth lifted to +10% to +13% (from +7/+10% set in February) and organic adjusted-EBITA margin expansion lifted to +70 to +100bps (from +50/+80bps), implying organic adjusted-EBITA growth of +14% to +19% and an implied margin of ~19.4-19.7% including scope and FX (vs ~19.1-19.4% in February). Cash conversion expected around 100%; effective tax rate 23-25% unchanged; FX impact of c.EUR -450/500m on FY revenue at current rates with negligible margin impact; restructuring charges peaking at ~EUR 450m in 2026 (unchanged total envelope). Mid-term CMD 2025 frame confirmed unchanged: +7% to +10% organic revenue growth per year and +250bps cumulative organic adj-EBITA margin expansion over 2026-2030, with ~100% average cash conversion.
pointsCles: Record H1 26: revenue EUR 21.2bn, +14.0% organic (Q2 +16.5%, best quarter ever at EUR 11.5bn) - Energy Management +15.4% (Q2 +18%) on data-center/AI demand with triple-digit semicon growth, Industrial Automation +7.7% (Q2 +11%) as discrete recovers and process turned positive; systems +28% in Q2 and the three largest markets (US, China, India) all growing around or above 20%.

Profitability inflection: adjusted EBITA EUR 4.1bn (+22% organic), margin 19.3% (+120bps organic; EM +100bps, IA +50bps) with gross margin 42.5% (+10bps) despite adverse systems mix - driven by EUR 535m industrial productivity, EUR 280m product pricing (price realization 2.5x in Q2 vs Q1, ~4pts of product growth) and SFC/sales down 1.1pt; net income EUR 2.5bn (+30%, IFRS basic EPS 4.42), record H1 FCF of EUR 1.6bn, ~100% FY cash conversion expected.

FY26 guidance RAISED on both axes at H1 (organic revenue to +10/13% from +7/10%; organic adj-EBITA margin expansion to +70/100bps from +50/80bps, i.e. +14/19% organic adj-EBITA growth) - management flags a tougher H2 productivity comparison base (>70% of FY25 productivity was delivered in H2), Middle East volatility and a c.EUR -450/500m FY FX headwind on revenue (negligible margin impact); EUR 100m Q2 tariff refunds flattered H1 (net tariff impact -104m in the bridge).

Portfolio and capacity acceleration for the AI cycle: Cognite (data foundation + Atlas AI agentic layer, signed pre-closing) and AiDASH acquisitions, Kraken grid-flexibility and SoftBank France AI-infrastructure partnerships (new prefab plant committed), Foxconn prefab capacity in North America, Motivair liquid cooling extended to Italy and India, high-density power-rack/power-center architectures in industrialization; IA turnaround on track toward 18% margin by 2028 (capitalized-R&D write-off taken, AVEVA subscription transition near completion); EUR 250m buybacks executed, restructuring to peak at ~EUR 450m in 2026.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Global leader in energy management (~83% of revenue: LV/MV distribution, datacenters, buildings, infrastructure) and industrial automation (~17%, incl. AVEVA software), riding a structural acceleration since 2023 on explosive datacenter demand (AI, hyperscalers). H1 2026 delivered a double guidance RAISE: organic revenue to +10/13% (from +7/10%) and adjusted-EBITA margin expansion to +70/100bp; H1 adjusted EPS 4.79, +28.5% organic.

== THESIS READ ==
- Datacenter demand is the engine and it is accelerating, not normalizing. Watch: Data Center & Networks order intake and backlog coverage.
- Margin expansion is guided AND raised - pricing plus mix, not just volume. Watch: Industrial Automation recovery (the lagging leg, AVEVA aside).
- Balance sheet carries the AVEVA-era debt (nd 13.7bn 2025); deleveraging to 8.5bn by 2030 modeled with light share creep (SBC), no big buyback assumed. Watch: capital-allocation signals.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base: 'ebit' = Adjusted EBITA (management's steering metric); 'net' = IFRS group share. The below-EBITA wedge (PPA amortization, restructuring, one-offs) is explicit in the bridge 'other' line (~-700M growing with scale); 2025 carried ~160M extra one-offs (documented residual). Historical series rebuilt from official Key-figures tables; shares derived from published adjusted EPS. priorEPS null (young fiche).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 44.3bn (raised guidance mid), adj EBITA 8.66bn (19.55% implied mid); 2027-2030: ~8.5%/yr revenue, margin +40bp/yr, ETR 26%, finNet declining with deleveraging. Watch: consensus (9.45 adjusted) vs Omnium 9.86 - Omnium sits ABOVE street on the raised frame; arbitrate at Q3.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 revenue (Oct); Capital Markets Day signals; datacenter capex prints from hyperscalers; Industrial Automation inflection.

ancrages.moteur: FY26 organic revenue growth guidance raised from 7-10% to 10-13% at the H1 26 release, after an H1 already at +14% organic (Q2 +16,5%). Midpoint taken (~11,5%) applied to FY25 revenue (40 152 M€), with FX/scope estimated slightly negative on the group's indications - FY26 revenue ~44,3 Md€, consistent with the post-H1 analyst consensus (~44,4 Md€, Simply Wall St).

FY26 adjusted EBITA margin guidance raised from +50-80bp to +70-100bp organic (implied margin ~19,4%-19,7% including scope/FX), with H1 26 having already delivered 19,3% (+120bp organic). Midpoint taken (~19,55%) applied to the FY26 revenue assumed.

Medium-term target from the 2025 Capital Markets Day (confirmed unchanged at H1 26): organic revenue growth +7% to +10%/yr (midpoint 8,5% taken for 2027-2030) and cumulative adjusted EBITA margin expansion of +250bp over 2026-2030 (of which the bulk of the 2026 raise itself already contributes, leaving ~+40bp/yr on average modelled for 2027-2030, taking the margin to ~21,15% in 2030).

Adjusted EBITA -> Adjusted Net Income (Group share) conversion held constant at the ratio observed in FY2025 (4 829 / 7 520 = 64,2%), applied identically across the whole projection horizon - a deliberate simplification that does not separately model the expected increase in net financial charges tied to the debt financing of the Cognite/AiDASH acquisitions (~3,45 Md$ in aggregate, closings not yet completed). Explicit point of caution, to be refined at the next refresh once these transactions have closed.

Temporary rise in net debt in 2026 tied to the debt financing of the Cognite (3,1 Md$) and AiDASH (~350 M$ EV) acquisitions announced at the end of June 2026 but not yet closed, partly offset by a still-high free cash flow (~5 Md€ estimated) and the absence of any other known major M&A transaction - deleveraging trajectory resuming from 2027 absent a new significant acquisition.

Slight and steady growth in the diluted share count (annual WESOP + OCEANE convertibles, partly offset by limited buybacks), consistent with the trend observed over 2021-2025 (~556M to ~562M shares), extrapolated at a similar pace (~+0,4%/yr) over the projection horizon.

Normative effective tax rate taken within the 23-25% range guided by management for FY26 (23,5% observed in FY25), implicitly embedded in the EBITA->Net conversion ratio held constant (see dedicated anchor) rather than modelled separately.
